question: The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the Earth is given by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**g = GM/R²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The formula for the **acceleration due to gravity** on the surface of the Earth is derived using **Newton's law of gravitation** and is given by **g = GM/R²**, where:

 
 
• **G** is the Universal Gravitational Constant (6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²).
 
• **M** is the mass of the Earth (~5.972 × 10²⁴ kg).
 
• **R** is the radius of the Earth (~6,371 km).
 
 
 
• The formula represents the gravitational acceleration experienced by an object on the surface of a spherical body like Earth.
 
• The value of **g** on the Earth's surface is approximately **9.8 m/s²**. This value varies slightly depending on altitude, latitude, and local geological conditions.
 
• Statement "**g = GM/R²**" is correct because it accurately represents the relationship between gravitational force and the distance from the Earth's center.
 
• Other options like "**g = GM**", "**g = GM/R**", and "**g = R²/GM**" are incorrect as they do not mathematically satisfy the laws of gravitation or dimensional analysis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gravitational Force:**

 
 
• The gravitational force between two masses is given by **F = GM₁M₂/r²**, where **r** is the distance between the centers of the two masses.
 
• This fundamental force is responsible for keeping celestial bodies like planets, moons, and satellites in their respective orbits.
 
 
 
• **Variation of g:**
 
 
• The value of **g** decreases with altitude as the distance **R** from the Earth's center increases.
 
• It also decreases with depth as the effective mass of the Earth contributing to the gravitational pull reduces.
 
• The Earth's rotation causes **g** to vary slightly with latitude. It is slightly higher at the poles and lower at the equator.
 
 
 
• **Applications of g:**
 
 
• The value of **g** is critical in various calculations like projectile motion, satellite motion, and free fall.
 
• It is used in designing structures and vehicles to ensure they can withstand gravitational forces.
 
 
 
• **Experimental Determination of g:**
 
 
• **Henry Cavendish's experiment** was one of the first to measure the gravitational constant, indirectly determining the value of **g**.
 
• Modern instruments like gravimeters are used to measure local variations in **g** for geological surveys.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Universal Gravitational Constant:** Its value remains the same throughout the universe and is a key constant in physics.
 
• **Dimensional Formula of g:** [L T⁻²]. This aligns with the formula **g = GM/R²**.
 
• **Space Missions:** Knowledge of **g** is critical for calculating escape velocity, orbital velocity, and designing space missions.
 
• **Earth's Shape:** The Earth is not a perfect sphere but an oblate spheroid, causing slight variations in **g**.
